column3: Close to the Hebrew; “Great” is rendered “prevalent.”
Close to the Hebrew; “His appetite” is rendered “his soul,” and “an evil affliction” as “a severe affliction.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB adds “proper” (“a proper burial”) and begins a quotation that runs through verse 6.
Close to the Hebrew; “Darkness” is rendered “obscurity.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Rest [belongs] to this one more than that one” is rendered “it is better off than he,” and NASB adds “anything.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB adds “the other man,” and “he did not see good” is rendered “does not enjoy good things.”
Close to the Hebrew; “His mouth” is kept, and “toil” is rendered “labor.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB repeats “What advantage” in the second question.
Close to the Hebrew; “The going of desire” is rendered “what the soul desires.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Contend” is rendered “dispute.”
Close to the Hebrew; “The number of the days of his life of futility” is rendered “the few years of his futile life.”
